literature_review.title: 19. Literature Review (self-loosening)
literature_review.content:
19. Literature review: self-loosening of bolted joints

What this review is, and what it is not. It is the literature this project engaged with and verified: the 29 sources whose curves form the validation corpus, the classics the field is built on, and the standards that define the tests. It is not an exhaustive survey of the subject. Every reference below carries a persistent identifier that was checked, or says explicitly why it has none. Section 21 lists them all.

19.1 Two loading directions, and why one dominates the literature

Work on threaded fasteners under vibration splits by how the joint is loaded. The earlier line is axial: Goodier and Sweeney (1945) tested axially loaded joints and described a partial-loosening mechanism in which pulsating tension produces radial sliding between thread flanks. The line that came to dominate practice is transverse: Junker's New Criteria for Self-Loosening of Fasteners Under Vibration (SAE, 1969) established transverse displacement as the severe condition and gave the field its test geometry, later codified as DIN 65151 and ISO 16130. Nearly every rig in this software's corpus is a Junker-type transverse rig or an axial force-controlled variant.

19.2 Rotational and non-rotational loosening

The literature separates loss of preload with nut rotation from loss without it. Pai and Hess mapped the rotational route in a pair of 2002 papers, one experimental and one a three-dimensional finite-element analysis, identifying localised slip at head and thread contacts as the trigger and showing that loosening can begin below the load a global-slip criterion would predict; they returned to the subject in 2004. Baek and co-workers (2019) treated the mechanism in complex structures. The non-rotational route is where embedding, creep and wear act: Basava and Hess (1998) measured clamping-force variation under axial vibration, and the Lakes group (2006) measured bolt load loss in aluminium joints held hot for a week, which is a creep measurement in the form this software calibrates against.

19.3 Analytical criteria

Nassar and Yang proposed a mathematical model for vibration-induced loosening of preloaded fasteners (2009), and Yang and Nassar followed it with a criterion for preventing self-loosening of preloaded cap screws under transverse cyclic excitation (2011). Criteria of this kind answer a different question from the one this software answers: they give a threshold for whether loosening occurs, where the model here integrates how much preload is lost over cycles.

19.4 Finite-element studies

Detailed contact models reproduce the mechanism at the cost of one joint per run. Jiang and co-workers published experimental and early-stage studies of self-loosening in 2003, Zhang and co-workers a finite-element model of it in 2004, and Izumi and co-workers a three-dimensional analysis of both tightening and loosening in 2005. The trade-off these papers make, fidelity against cost, is the reason a lumped-parameter model is worth having: it is the regime between a decay law fitted to one joint and a finite-element run per condition.

19.5 Recent modelling and reviews

Gong and co-workers (2020) analysed the mechanism through a modified Iwan model, and their review of anti-loosening methods surveys the countermeasure literature. The corpus of this software draws mostly on work published from 2016 onward, which is where transverse-rig data with enough reported detail to be read back from figures becomes common.

19.6 Standards

Five standards frame the measurements and the design rules used here: DIN 65151 and ISO 16130 for the transverse test, ISO 16047 for torque/clamp force, ISO 724 for thread geometry, and VDI 2230 for joint calculation. A standard has no DOI: its code is its identifier.

19.7 Where this software sits

The model implements four loss mechanisms in parallel, embedding, creep, fretting wear and nut rotation, with a surface-damage state that modulates friction and wear, and it is confronted with 210 digitised curves from the 29 sources of Section 20. None of those curves was measured by the authors of this software: each is read from a figure or a table of the cited publication. The per-source blocks in Section 20 give the citation, the DOI and the apparatus as the source described it.

validation_sources.title: 20. Validation Sources (29 papers)
validation_sources.content:
20. Validation sources: one block per paper

The corpus draws on 29 sources. For each one: the citation as the apparatus note records it, the DOI, how many curves were digitised from it, the median mean absolute error of the model on those curves, and the apparatus as the source described it. The saved models of every curve are in Models/SAVED_CASES/<SOURCE>/.

20.1 BAUER_2024 (9 curves)

Bauer 2024 (Eng. Fail. Anal.) — accumulation of preload loss, M8 + M12x1.5

Bauer et al. (TU Darmstadt), "Method of accumulation of preload loss of bolted joints due to rotational self-loosening caused by cyclic, transversal excitation", Engineering Failure Analysis 162 (2024) 108404.

DOI: 10.1016/j.engfailanal.2024.108404

Median mean absolute error on these curves: 0.0420

Apparatus, as reported:

  • Junker-type transverse-displacement test rig (DIN 65151 family), displacement-controlled;
  • Continuous preload F_V measurement via load washer; run-out 20,000 cycles; loosening
  • Excitation frequency given only symbolically (s(t)=s_a·sin(2πf·t)) — no numeric Hz.
  • Headline result: critical local slip amplitude **s_crit ≈ 76–108 µm (99 µm at

Saved models: Models/SAVED_CASES/BAUER_2024/ (9 .msd)

20.2 CACCESE_2009 (7 curves)

Caccese et al. 2009 (Composite Structures) + Pelletier/Caccese/Berube 2005 (DTIC ADA429921) — Influence of stress relaxation on clamp-up force in hybrid composite-to-metal bolted joints

Caccese et al. (2009). Compos. Struct. 89:285-293

DOI: 10.1016/j.compstruct.2008.07.031

Median mean absolute error on these curves: 0.0220

Saved models: Models/SAVED_CASES/CACCESE_2009/ (7 .msd)

Saved models: Models/SAVED_CASES/CHU_2026/ (9 .msd)

jcsr2023 — Loss of preload of unprotected bolted joints considering environmental effects

Yang, Bai & Ding (2023). JCSR 211:108211

Median mean absolute error on these curves: 0.0118

20.8 KARLSEN_2022 (11 curves)

Karlsen & Lemu 2022 (Eng. Fail. Anal.) — M30/M42, HV vs Vibralock

Karlsen & Lemu, "Comparative study on loosening of anti-loosening bolt and standard bolt system", Engineering Failure Analysis (2022).

DOI: 10.1016/j.engfailanal.2022.106590

Median mean absolute error on these curves: 0.0314

Apparatus, as reported:

  • Large-scale Junker-type transverse vibration rig for very large bolts, 1 Hz,
  • Preload measured continuously (load cell washer stack); preload applied either by
  • Comparison: standard HV nut system vs Vibralock(R) anti-loosening system.
  • Run-out ~3,000–3,100 cycles for surviving (Vibralock) runs.

Saved models: Models/SAVED_CASES/KARLSEN_2022/ (11 .msd)

20.9 LIU_2016 (14 curves)

Liu, Ouyang, Feng, Cai, Liu, Zhu, "Study on self-loosening of bolted joints excited by dynamic axial load", Tribology International 115 (2017) 432–451.

DOI: 10.1016/j.triboint.2017.05.037

Median mean absolute error on these curves: 0.0180

Apparatus, as reported:

  • Axial (tension) dynamic-load excitation on a fatigue testing machine, 30 Hz, in air
  • Clamp force measured with a load cell in the clamped stack (in series with the joint);
  • Preload applied with a digital electronic torque wrench to a set clamp-force value.
  • Post-test residual (breakaway) torque also recorded (Figs 5a/8a — not digitized).

Saved models: Models/SAVED_CASES/LIU_2017_AXIAL/ (9 .msd)

DOI: 10.1016/j.wear.2020.203453

Median mean absolute error on these curves: 0.0133

Apparatus, as reported:

  • Rig: lower plate fixed to the testing platform; a load cell (WTP
  • Control mode: displacement-controlled (the machine imposes a cyclic
  • Preload application: torque wrench (static, pre-test); no torque control
  • Frequency: 5 Hz, fixed across the whole study (not swept).

Saved models: Models/SAVED_CASES/LIU_2020_WEAR/ (9 .msd)

20.12 LIU_2022_RETIGHT (21 curves)

Z. Liu 2022 (Structures) — retightening (reaperto) after loosening, M12

DOI: 10.1016/j.istruc.2022.08.049

Median mean absolute error on these curves: 0.0149

Saved models: Models/SAVED_CASES/LIU_2022_RETIGHT/ (21 .msd)

20.13 LIU_2025 (7 curves)

Liu 2025 (Sci. Rep.) — M16 transverse loosening-life tests

Liu et al., "Bolt loosening evaluation method based on normalized screw root equivalent stress and loosening life curve", Scientific Reports 15 (2025).

DOI: 10.1038/s41598-025-02936-6

Median mean absolute error on these curves: 0.0339

Apparatus, as reported:

  • Transverse (shear) displacement-controlled loosening test on a servo test machine;
  • PTFE/lubricating-oil treatment on fixture contact faces to remove parasitic fixture
  • Load train (series): bolt → small gasket → fixture → **EVT-14 TP-12T pressure (clamp-force)
  • Preload applied with a torque wrench, controlled against the pressure sensor reading.

Saved models: Models/SAVED_CASES/LIU_2025/ (7 .msd)

20.14 LI_2022_MARSTRUC (6 curves)

Y. Li 2022 (Marine Structures) — contact-creep clamping-force relaxation, M16

Y. Li et al., "A combined theoretical and experimental study on contact creep-induced clamping force relaxation of bolted joints at ambient temperature", Marine Structures 85 (2022) 103263.

DOI: 10.1016/j.marstruc.2022.103263

Median mean absolute error on these curves: 0.0037

Saved models: Models/SAVED_CASES/LI_2022_MARSTRUC/ (6 .msd)

20.15 LI_2022_TRIBOINT (4 curves)

H. Li 2022 (Tribology Int.) — frequency effect on axial-excitation loosening, M10

H. Li et al., "Effect of frequency on the fatigue performance of bolted joints under axial excitation", Tribology International 176 (2022) 107933.

DOI: 10.1016/j.triboint.2022.107933

Median mean absolute error on these curves: 0.0323

Saved models: Models/SAVED_CASES/LI_2022_TRIBOINT/ (4 .msd)

20.16 LU_2024 (13 curves)

Lu/Yang 2024 (Sensors) — M8 tangential pre-loading relaxation

Lu, Yang et al., "Prediction of Pre-Loading Relaxation of Bolt Structure of Complex Equipment under Tangential Cyclic Load", Sensors 24(11):3306 (2024).

DOI: 10.3390/s24113306

Median mean absolute error on these curves: 0.0337

Apparatus, as reported:

  • 50 kN electro-hydraulic servo fatigue testing machine (Xi'an make), software-controlled,
  • Ring force sensor in the bolt stack for clamp-force measurement; zeroed before
  • Clamped members: nickel steel flat plates, surface roughness variants Ra 0.8 / 1.6 / 3.2 µm.

Saved models: Models/SAVED_CASES/LU_2024/ (13 .msd)

Qin et al. 2024 (Appl Compos Mater) — Preload Relaxation of CFRP Bolted Joints Under Thermal-Oxygen Environment

Qin et al. (2024). Appl. Compos. Mater. 31

DOI: 10.1007/s10443-024-10214-3

Rousseau & Bouzid 2025 (Materials) — clamped-member material & thickness, M12

Rousseau & Bouzid, "Effect of Clamped Member Material and Thickness on Bolt Self-Loosening Under Transverse Loads", Materials 18(2):462 (2025).

Apparatus, as reported:

  • Two clamped members of equal thickness + bolt + nut + two washers (2.4 mm each).
